appointment-type.title: What would you like to discuss?

options.hint: Divorce and dissolution can be complicated and stressful. Getting impartial guidance from us can make managing your pension options easier.

radio-button.error: Select what type of appointment you would like.

sections.content: A free Pension Wise appointment explains the options for taking money from your defined contribution pension. It’s impartial and backed by government.
You’ll find out:
items: when you can access your pension pots
the different ways you can take money from your pension
how each option is usually taxed
how to spot and avoid scams.

sections.content: You can’t book a Pension Wise appointment if:
items: you’re under 50
you only have a defined benefit pension (final salary or career-average salary) or
you only have an overseas pension.

sections.content: If you’re self-employed, pension options can feel complicated and hard to compare. This appointment helps you understand how pensions work when you work for yourself, and what your choices are.
You’ll find out:
items: the types of pensions available to self-employed people
how contributions work and what you can afford to save
how tax relief is applied and what you could get back
what to consider when choosing a pension provider or scheme
how to check your state pension forecast
how to spot risks and avoid pension scams
where to get free, impartial guidance if you need more help

sections.content: You **can’t** book a Self-employed appointment if:
items: you aren’t self-employed

sections.content:
Our divorce and separation section is here to give you all the guidance you need when it comes to managing your finances during a relationship break-up.

It doesn’t matter what your situation is. You may be divorcing or separating; have children or not; own your home or rent; or live in England, Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland. We have guides that will cover your specific situation.

Divorce and dissolution can be complicated and stressful. Getting impartial guidance from us can make managing your pension options easier.

During your appointment, you'll speak with one of our pension specialists who will:
items: explain the pension options available during a divorce/dissolution
help you understand what to consider and the questions to ask
guide you on your next steps, including where to find additional help and how to access regulated financial advice if needed.

sections.content: You **can’t** book a divorce and separation appointment if:
items: you have agreed a financial settlement in the divorce proceedings

sections.content:
There is scams support out there, but it can be overwhelming to navigate when you’ve been scammed. It can also come at a price that people cannot afford.

That’s why we have a specialist free Pension Loss service. Our pension specialists help consumers to make sense of what has happened and all the bewildering acronyms. We discuss the possible redress options and provide helpful resources at no charge. This can be enough to enable a scams victim to approach the right organisations to recover at least some of the money they have lost.
You’ll find out:
items: what has happened to your pension and what it means for you
what common scam-related pension terms and acronyms refer to
what options you may have to recover some of the money you’ve lost
what to expect next, including possible investigations or follow-up steps

sections.content: You **can’t** book a pension loss appointment if:
items: you have not been the victim of a suspected or confirmed pension scam

sections.content:
You’ve been referred by your pension provider for a free Pension Safeguarding Guidance appointment to talk about the transfer of your pension benefits.

Keep in mind that this appointment is to help you understand the risk of being scammed and avoid making a transfer that leads to you losing some or all of your pension savings.

You must attend the appointment yourself. Appointments cannot be attended by someone acting on your behalf.

If you plan on consolidating more than one pension then please wait until you have requested all transfers before booking your appointment. This will avoid being asked to attend more than one safeguarding appointment.

If you don’t think you need this appointment, please contact your pension provider.

sections.title: What an appointment covers
sections.content: You’ll find out:
items: Things to consider before moving a pension, for example loss of any special features, investments, security, fees and charges.
How to spot and avoid a scam.

sections.content: You **can’t** book a safeguarding appointment if:
items: you haven’t been referred by the pension provider you’re seeking a transfer from

ds.title: What you need for your divorce and separation appointment

sections.content: So we can understand your plans for retirement, we’ll usually ask you about your pensions and other finances. You’ll usually benefit more from a divorce and separation appointment if, before your appointment, you:
Ask each of your pension providers:
items: how much your pension is currently worth
if your pension has any special features, like a guaranteed pot value or annuity rate.

sections.content: Check your State Pension forecast:
items: [online on GOV.UK (opens in a new tab)](https://www.gov.uk/check-state-pension)
call [0800 731 0175](tel:08007310175) between 8am and 6pm, Monday to Friday.

sections.content: Have details of your other finances, like:
items: savings and investments
debts and repayments.

sections.content: Think about your plans for retirement, such as:
items: when you’d like to stop working
what type of pension income you’d like.

sections.content: On the next screen, you will be prompted to book your appointment date and time, but be mindful of having time to collate the information above to get the most out of your appointment.

psg.title: What you need for your Pension Safeguarding appointment

sections.content: During the appointment, you’ll be asked for details of the pension transfer you’re making and your financial situation. In order to provide the most beneficial guidance and to tailor your appointment to your personal circumstances, it’s helpful if you can find out:
items: The type of pension you already have – usually defined contribution or defined benefit – and the name of the product, like a personal or workplace pension.
The type and name of the pension scheme you want to transfer to.
The fees and charges for both schemes.

If you are transferring a defined contribution pension, how each scheme plans to invest your money, including the funds or types of asset they use – you can ask each pension provider if you’re not sure.
Any details provided by your current pension provider as to the reason for requiring an appointment.  They may refer to their reasons as a red or amber flag.
Details of any financial adviser you’ve used.

sections.content: **It’s also useful to:**
items: Have information about all the sources of retirement income you might have, including other pensions.
Think about your plans for retirement, including when you want to start taking your pension and when you’d like to stop working or reduce your hours.

sections.content: On the next screen, you will be prompted to book your appointment date and time, but be mindful of having time to collate the information above to get the most out of your appointment.

access-support.title: Would you like any adjustments for your appointment?

sections.content: A standard PensionWise appointment will be via telephone and last for approximately 1 hour. We can make adjustments to meet your needs. For example, you can ask for:
items: A Welsh-speaking pension specialist
A British Sign Language interpreter
A foreign language interpreter
Someone to attend the appointment with you
Adjustments for accessibility needs

sections.title: How the appointment will take place
sections.content: Your appointment will take place as a video call. This means:
items: the pension specialist will join the video call
a BSL interpreter will join the video call
you will be given a link to join the video call

sections.content: The interpreter will translate between you and the pension specialist during the appointment.

access-companion.title: Having someone attend your appointment with you

sections.content: This page explains how your appointment will work if you want someone to attend with you.

sections.title: If someone will join your appointment remotely
sections.content:
If the other person cannot be with you in person - for example, if they have Power of Attorney or live far away,  they can join the appointment remotely.

Your appointment will take place as a **conference call**. This means:
items: you will join the appointment as usual
the pension specialist will join the call by telephone
the person supporting you can join the call remotely
we will provide details on how they can join the call after you book

sections.content: The person supporting you will be able to listen and speak during the appointment.

sections.title: If someone will be with you in the same room
sections.content:
If the person supporting you will be with you during the appointment - for example, a carer, family member or friend, they can sit with you while you join the call.

They do not need separate joining instructions unless you request them.

cancel your appointment

sections.content:
If you need to change any personal details you have provided, you will need to call us on [0800 138 3944](tel:08001383944) ([+44 20 3733 3495](tel:+442037333495) if you're outside the UK) or use the [webchat](#).

We're open between 9am and 5pm, Monday to Friday. Closed on bank holidays.
